evidence.quotation: When a Trap Card is activated: Pay 1000 LP; negate the activation, and if you do, destroy it.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current reference semantics. No original printed-text verification. Corroborate the activation/effect distinction with the curated Goat Seven Tools ruling.

evidence.quotation: The effects are then resolved, starting at the top link and working down to the Chain Link 1 at the bottom.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Period baseline for reverse resolution; does not establish every individual card ruling.

evidence.quotation: the same player can play consecutive cards if their opponent does not respond
evidence.historicalApplicability: Period baseline for responding to one’s own Trap after the opponent declines; response priority is still checked.

evidence.quotation: Only another Spell Speed 3 card may be used against these cards.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Counter Trap baseline. Speed alone does not satisfy a responding card activation condition. Counter-to-counter responses can be legal, but are outside the proposed first scope.

evidence.quotation: These cards can be used against a card with a Spell Speed of 1 or 2.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Normal Trap is listed in this section. Preserve the existing speed-2 Trap Hole behavior; do not allow it to respond to speed 3.

evidence.quotation: Paying a cost means an action like discarding or sending a card to the Graveyard from your hand, or paying Life Points, in order to Summon a monster or activate an effect. You have to pay any costs before you declare the activation of the card.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Period baseline that paying LP can be a cost; the specific fixed amount comes from Seven Tools current reference text.

evidence.quotation: Even if the activation of the card is negated, you cannot get a refund of the cost that you have paid.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Already paid costs remain paid. First scope does not implement a further Counter negating Seven Tools; no-refund remains a requirement for any later extension.

evidence.quotation: For an effect that targets a card, you select the target that you would like and then activate the effect.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Baseline distinction between choosing a card target and recording the Chain link being answered. Seven Tools non-targeting design is a semantic reading of current reference text/direct-chain supplement, not a quotation explicitly stating that property.

evidence.quotation: Before you can activate a Trap Card, you must Set it on the field first.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current common Trap baseline under the selected Goat policy. No hand-activation exception is enabled.

evidence.quotation: You cannot activate a Trap in the same turn that you Set it, but you can activate it at any time after that
evidence.historicalApplicability: Read together with each Trap condition and response priority; not permission to activate Seven Tools at arbitrary timing.

evidence.quotation: if a general rule is not explicitly listed here is being different in Goat Format, you can assume that it works the exact same way as it does in the current format.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Existing community policy adopted by the project; retain its editorial caveat about recent rule changes.

evidence.quotation: They cannot choose to pay if it would make their Life Points become 0.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Community transcription of a period LP-payment rule. This is an Imperial Order example, not a Seven Tools-specific original bulletin; combine with the activation-cost example and Seven Tools fixed 1000 cost.

evidence.quotation: “Injection Fairy Lily’s” effect may not be activated if the controller’s Life Points are at or below 2000.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Period activation-cost example corroborating that an exact fixed LP cost cannot be paid down to zero. Derive Seven Tools minimum 1001 from its fixed 1000 cost; do not enable Lily or its battle effect.

evidence.quotation: “Seven Tools of the Bandit” may not be activated in a chain to the use of an effect of a continuous Trap that has already been activated, like “Ultimate Offering.”
evidence.historicalApplicability: Curated period distinction between Trap card activation and a previously active Continuous Trap effect. Ultimate Offering and Continuous Trap handling remain unsupported.

evidence.quotation: ■自分または相手の罠カードのカードの発動に直接チェーンして発動するカードです。（カードの発動を伴わない、罠カードの効果の発動にチェーンして発動することはできません。）
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current OCG corroboration: directly chain to one’s own or the opponent’s Trap card activation, not an effect activation without card activation. Not asserted as original TCG 2005 wording.

evidence.quotation: When a Spell Card is activated: Discard 1 card; negate the activation, and if you do, destroy it.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current reference semantics, cross-checked with the curated Goat Magic Jammer entries. Not an original printed-text verification.

evidence.quotation: Counter trap used against Chain Link 3.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Period example explicitly includes a Counter Trap responding to a previous Counter Trap. It does not itself identify Seven Tools or prove every speed-3 response is legal.

evidence.quotation: Spell and Trap Cards remain on the field until the entire chain resolves, unless destroyed by a card effect during the chain.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Community transcription of a period FAQ, not an authenticated original UDE bulletin. Distinguishes normal Chain-end cleanup from Magic Jammer destroyed immediately by Seven Tools. Stamping Destruction remains unsupported.

evidence.quotation: Then the effect of “Heavy Storm” (Chain Link 1) is resolved successfully, destroying all Spell and Trap Cards on the field,
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current official three-link example corroborates that negating link 2 does not negate link 1. The example uses a Normal Trap, not Magic Jammer; counter-to-counter applicability is derived with the archived speed diagram and Seven Tools Trap activation condition. Example cards remain outside runtime.

evidence.quotation: The order of the cards in the Graveyard should not be changed.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current official baseline for preserving Graveyard order. This statement does not specify the relative order of multiple Spell/Trap sources placed in the Graveyard at Chain end; that implementation check remains pending.

evidence.quotation: 一つの効果処理にて、一度に複数のカードが同時に墓地へ送られる事になる場合、それらのカードを墓地へ置く順番は、その墓地へ送られるカードの持ち主が選ぶ事ができます。
evidence.historicalApplicability: Official ownership/ordering principle for simultaneous cards sent by one effect. Chain-end cleanup is a rules action, so its application there is a synthesis with the general community rule and simultaneous-cleanup sources, not a direct quotation about cleanup.

evidence.quotation: デュエル中に墓地へ送られたカードの順番を、プレイヤーが任意に入れ替える事はできません。
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current baseline: ordering newly sent cards does not authorize rearranging cards already in the GY.

evidence.quotation: 墓地に送られたカードは、墓地に送られた順番のままでデュエルを進行します。
evidence.historicalApplicability: Preserve established GY order. Previously paid discard, destroyed Magic Jammer and root-effect victims are outside the later cleanup batch.

evidence.quotation: 最後にチェーン処理が終了し、発動した「フォースフィールド」と「神罰」は墓地へ送られる事になります。
evidence.historicalApplicability: Official Counter example corroborates deferred cleanup. No Minerva/Counter-trigger support, fourth link or example-card import is enabled.

evidence.quotation: また、その一連のチェーンが全て終了したタイミングで、ルールによって全て同時に墓地へ送られるので、「チェーン処理の最中は魔法＆罠ゾーンにこれらの使用済みカードは存在し続けている」ことになります。
evidence.historicalApplicability: Community statement explicitly supplies simultaneity of normal Chain-end cleanup. Apply only to sources that remain to be cleaned up; a source already destroyed in the Chain is excluded.

evidence.quotation: 複数枚のカードが同時に墓地へ送られる場合、カードの持ち主が墓地に置く順番を決定します。
evidence.historicalApplicability: General community formulation for simultaneous sends, corroborated for a specific effect by official FAQ 206. Not represented as an authenticated TCG 2005 bulletin.

evidence.quotation: また、自分で発動したカードでも、相手が発動したカードでも、墓地に置く順番を決定するプレイヤーは、墓地へ送られるカードの持ち主になります。
evidence.historicalApplicability: Order within one GY belongs to the card owner. Do not give a counter/effect controller permission to reorder another player’s batch.

evidence.quotation: When your opponent Normal or Flip Summons a monster with 1000 or more ATK: Target that monster; destroy that target.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Current semantics reference; 2002 LOB print evidence separate. Not claiming 2005 printed wording.

evidence.quotation: “Trap Hole” is a targeting effect.
evidence.historicalApplicability: Goat compilation labels this Netrep ruling. Community source, not authenticated original UDE publication.

quotations.locator: printed p.32, Opponent’s Chance to Respond

evidence.quotation: When making a play on a Chain, you must always ask your opponent, "Do you wish to continue?"
evidence.historicalApplicability: Period-looking archived rulebook baseline for giving the opponent a response opportunity. Not publisher authentication, not a complete Goat priority/SEGOC specification.

decisions.conclusion: M responds directly to S; V responds directly to latest T/M/V card activation.
decisions.rationale: Card condition plus Speed 3 and latest-link requirement; subtype/speed alone is insufficient.
decisions.limitations: No monster effect, Continuous Trap effect-only activation or Spell directly answered by Seven.

decisions.conclusion: T^k shares one eligible opponent Normal/Tribute/Flip Summon, then only V may extend it.
decisions.rationale: Combine existing Trap Hole condition/targeting with Speed 2 response to Speed 2. During building, earlier T has not resolved and the same target is still present. Once V is added, Speed 2 cannot follow it.
decisions.limitations: Synthesis, not a quoted TCG-2005 FAQ for multiple Trap Hole plus Seven. Do not bypass pending Trigger or add new Summon windows.

decisions.conclusion: Opponent has first response opportunity; own responses require a decline. Every Trap source was Set before this turn.
decisions.rationale: Retain the existing Main1/Main2 priority/pass and earlier-Set policy.
decisions.limitations: No new ignition priority, SEGOC, Damage Step or phase timing rules.

decisions.conclusion: Resolve backwards; V cancels only the immediately preceding activation, which is then skipped. Other earlier links continue.
decisions.rationale: Alternating Counter cancellations follow repeated direct responses; no hard-coded odd/even board patch.
decisions.limitations: Odd/even is an oracle consequence, not proof of a new exact-length official example.

decisions.conclusion: Cancelling the last T does not cancel earlier T. Earlier T may destroy the same monster; later checks never retarget or send an already departed target again.
decisions.rationale: Every T fixes its target at activation; resolve each surviving link independently against current target identity/location.
decisions.limitations: Only the one Summon target and existing pool; no simultaneous multi-Summon, protection, replacement or control changes.

decisions.conclusion: Each accepted V costs 1000 with LP >1000; M discards one card; reject before mutation when unpayable. Never refund committed costs.
decisions.rationale: LP >1000 combines fixed printed cost with the adopted rule against choosing a payment that makes LP zero.
decisions.limitations: No reducers, prevention, half-LP costs or LP-payment triggers.

decisions.conclusion: Negated/destroyed sources leave immediately; remaining used sources wait to Chain end, then each owner orders its own simultaneous batch. Preserve old Graveyard order.
decisions.rationale: Retain the adopted cleanup policy: combine official current examples/owner-order principle with community rules-action descriptions.
decisions.limitations: FAQ 206 is about one effect, not direct rules cleanup authority. This is project synthesis, not a newly authenticated TCG-2005 cleanup ruling.

decisions.conclusion: At most 8 links for these families with this pool; validate per-owner copies and occupied slots, not just total length.
decisions.rationale: Three copies of Seven per owner and five Spell/Trap slots per player; no Trap revival/control-changing effect in the pool.
decisions.limitations: Eight is not a Yu-Gi-Oh! Chain limit. Revisit bounds before future cards/custom effects.

decisions.conclusion: Historical costs remain valid after root heal/movement; a current-board binding must be refreshed by a trusted parent.
decisions.rationale: Keep C2a/C2b distinction and server-only receipts/journals.
decisions.limitations: Hashes are not authentication; candidate snapshots are not legal action histories.

decisions.conclusion: Root runs once, may pause for its private choice, then survivor cleanup; terminal/concede never invent post-game owner choices.
decisions.rationale: Keep current single-source versus multi-source terminal bookkeeping and adapter dedup/version contract.
decisions.limitations: Engineering policy, not a universal new rule for every effect after a Duel ends.

decisions.conclusion: Activation target cannot be a card discarded by later M; source/target/link/decision identity stays pinned through resume.
decisions.rationale: Root target selection precedes later Counter costs; an instance cannot be retroactively selected from a future zone.

decisions.conclusion: Only install the proposed v6 after actual activation/frame/discovery/UI/regression checks; v1-v5 artifacts remain historical.
decisions.rationale: Review supports implementation, not runtime enablement. Preserve imported metadata and old decks/artwork.
decisions.limitations: Candidates/evidence checks do not count as live effects or Windows 11 desktop evidence.
